schema: Qualitative assistant analysis, not human adjudication; external ratings remain immutable. caught=plausibly relevant recorded rejection, partial=nonlocalizing risk signal, missed=no relevant recorded rejection. No causal attribution to an individual NLI span is established.

cases.analysis: certainty rejects might/may by exact token-set equality; future_tense rejects will/can. The reviewer accepts the core meaning, but will/can also weakens modality, so this is not an unqualified technical FP.
cases.o: will make you look around for a long time
cases.n: can make you hesitate for a long time

cases.future_action: Document uncertainty and seek targeted review before any modal-equivalence relaxation.
cases.reviewer_disagreement: Prediction will becomes possibility can; keenly desired loses keenly. Keep external Yes unchanged; these are new assistant-identified risks, not adjudicated drift.

cases.analysis: The reviewer accepts the same necessity, calendar timing and war-on-Christmas framing. Have to becomes must; CERT recognizes only must.

cases.analysis: The only rejecting guard compares digit strings; the quantity ten weeks equals 10 weeks. The external reviewer explicitly treats this as formatting only.
cases.guard_relevance: numbers rejection is technical for this span, not evidence of a changed quantity. No threshold issue.

cases.reviewer_disagreement: The whole rewrite also changes most to many and drops sharply; these are separate quantifier/intensity risks the supplied review did not mention. Formatting-only applies to 10/ten, not blanket approval of the row.

cases.analysis: External TN and all checks pass, but close reading raises an actor-role contradiction not recognized by the supplied review.

cases.reviewer_disagreement: The original wants these sailors to fight one's wars; the rewrite wants to face them as opponents. This is a candidate role reversal, not a change to the saved external label.
